It's a zama zama

By: Chwayitisa Futshane | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
we go inside the world of illegal mining, from mining gold nuggets to selling them on the black market, to the Kingpins who really benefit from the illegal gold trade.

Summary:
It's one of the most dangerous jobs on earth but for many illegal miners, it's their only means of income.

This week, with exclusive footage from an abandoned mine in Durban Deep Informal Settlement, Carte Blanche traces the lengths that illegal miners will go to find gold and we also find out who's really benefiting from the illegal gold trade.

Extra Budget Items:
Hiring a car from Budget for safety reasons for the shoot.

Payment for McDonald - the Freelance journalist who shot the underground footage in the mines and who is also working on the research for the story. GM decided on a daily rate of R2500 for a maximum of 5 days.

Press Release:


Black Market Mining
Crawling through tiny underground tunnels and breathing in toxic dust for days on end, theirs is one of the most dangerous jobs on earth. But it’s so lucrative that illegal miners are willing to risk life and limb to unearth tiny specks of gold to sell on. Carte Blanche delves into the world of the so-called Zama Zamas who infiltrate abandoned gold mines to supply the black market trade.


Script:


UPSOUND:
Brig Mulaudzi - 02:43:34: We’re going to the suspect’s house where we will be affecting arrests on the two suspects we have identified.


VO: Early on Friday the 29th of May, specialised crime busting unit The Hawks, entered a high security estate in Kempton Park, looking for suspects believed to be members of an illegal gold trade syndicate.


VO: The HAWKS confiscated bags of gold-rich soil and gold processing equipment, at one of the homes in this security estate
These bags of gold-rich soil, were illegally mined from the depths of the earth by desperate miners living in abject poverty.


VO: With exclusive access to an abandoned mine in Durban Deep Informal Settlement, we tracked the lengths that illegal miners will go to, to find gold.

LINK 18:23:55:15 - It’s just a rubbish dump to you and me but to others, it’s a gold mine, quite literally because through that hole in the ground, hundreds of illegal miners enter, in search of gold.


VO: At an abandoned gold mine near Roodepoort, we followed Freelance photographer McDonald Mahlatlole to the entrance of this concealed, underground world.

He risked his life filming zama zamas for several days as they went to work, digging for gold.

UPSOUND
I was scared at first, but I told myself that I want to see what these people are doing, how do they get this money...
There’s no protection, you just have to take your headlamp or a device that can maybe take you out. Because it’s extremely dark


VO: But as terrifying as it was for McDonald, this is a way of life for Zama zamas.


UPSOUND: Tjovis
18:07:59:05 ... an accident is always waiting to happen, and if it’s meant to happen, it will happen because at the end of the day this is illegal, it is a zama zama. If you die, you die, it’s do or die.


VO: Every day illegal miners set off for work just like ordinary people. The only difference is, these men risk life and limb for the chance to make a few hundred rands.

We’ve seen it before on Carte Blanche... illegal miners being pulled out of abandoned mine shafts after a rock fall.

Rasta has been an illegal miner for many years.

He started illegally mining gold back in his home country Zimbabwe but he came to South Africa looking for ways to make an honest living.


UPSOUND:

TCR: 05:54:06:14

Rasta: We were very poor and that forced me to join them without a second thought. So I joined them.


VO: He explains how they find the right abandoned mines to work in.


UPSOUND:

06:00:47:00 - RASTA: We go into mines that are abandoned, that were left behind a long time ago by previous owners. Those that have already been closed, we come and we open them ourselves. We open all the caves, and we look and see what the safety setup is.


VO: Long before any gold can be excavated from these abandoned mines, the zama zama’s must manoeuvre through hazardous tunnels and passages.

There are hours of crawling, moving between cracks in the mine and climbing up and down rocks.


UPSOUND:

06:02:30:21- Rasta: ... We just go down and when we get there, there is no place to stand up straight. It means that I need to be on my knees or I must sit down where I’m working. In other areas we crawl on our stomachs. There are these tiny openings which we need to go through, but if my head can go through, then I can go through.


VO: Once they find a gold-rich area in the mine, they sift the soil before panning it for gold particles.
Then they begin digging, filling up sacks with up to 30 kilograms of soil.
All of this happens while they’re underground.
Then it’s the long haul back, carrying the heavy sacks to the surface.


LINK 18:52:18:03 - Life at Durban Deep informal settlement is grim and bleak, folks live here on the very edge of existence, manyare unemployed and unskilled.

And In the midst of this poverty you either become a zama zamas or you benefit from the work of the illegal miners.

VO: Once the miners are back on the surface and just a few hundred metres from the abandoned mines, men and women gather to grind the soil and stones brought up from the mine, into fine dust.
It’s this dust that contains gold particles.
The workers here are paid by the illegal miners to grind and wash the soil and they can earn as little as R100 a day, for their efforts.


Rasta: (06:11:30:00) Some of them want R100 for crushing, others want the soil that we have already washed ...


VO: This is because there’s always a chance that even after the soil has been processed; it could contain even more gold particles.
Using a bucket of water and a small amount of mercury, the crushed stone is processed over and over again, with the mercury pulling together the tiny particles of gold to make these nuggets.
Once this process is done, the gold nuggets are ready to be sold to the buyers.


UPSOUND RASTA: TCR: 06:07:35:06

The people that buy live here in there shacks.


AERIAL SHOT before Thabang walking shot...


VO: Thabang is a buyer.
His business brings in thousands of rands, from buying illegal gold from the zama zamas.



SOUNDUP THABANG: 18:30:49:00 It depends on the number of customers that come in... like last month, I didn’t work hard enough and I only got R15000.


VO: Many zama zamas live here with their families in these informal structures, which are usually no bigger than four square metres.

So any form of income is fiercely protected.


VO:
We spent months trying to gain the trust of the zama zamas. In the end, we were able to persuade one of them to go inside and make the sale.


VO: It’s a simple enough operation. A zama zama takes this little gold nugget to the buyer, where the gold is weighed on a small scale and depending on the size of the nugget; the miner gets his pay.


THABANG 18:27:31:13 - I buy from the zama zamas. I buy from them sometimes for R360, R370, R380. It depends on what my spot price calculation is.


VO: To calculate his spot price, Thabang undercuts the current trading value of gold, which is around R470 per gram, by at least R100.
So we did the maths.
With the buyers’ average price of a gram of gold at around R370, a zama zama who gets five grams of gold, makes about R1850.


VO: And after what they say is good pay day, they celebrate.


TCR: 06:09:39:00

Rasta: It depends on you and what you’re aiming for. There are those who want R3000 and then there are those who want R200 and there are those who want to get R12000 here.


LINK: Now you might be asking yourself, what does all this have to do with you?



VO: Luther Lebelo, the spokesperson for the South African Revenue Services, explains how the illegal gold trade, has a direct impact on the tax payer.


UPSOUND LUTHER LEBELO: [04:59] ...This illicit trade fits into the broader tax gap of SARS. For instance, this one in particular, the research that we’ve made is that over three years, it has cost SARS or the tax gap over R5 billion, which is quite a lot of money.


VO: In September last year we exposed this elaborate money making scam.

Illegally mined gold is bought through gold traders , from zama zamas.

This pure gold is melted down and mixed with metals such as copper. This reduces the quality of the gold, which is then used to make second hand jewellery.

Members of this syndicate then forge paperwork to make it appear as though, this gold actually comes from second-hand jewellery stores.

Once the gold is disguised and sold with the fraudulent paperwork, it can easily pass into the legal gold trade.

But it doesn’t end there.

This entire scam is ‎funded through fraudulent VAT claims made to SARS.

And this is what makes it so lucrative.

SARS has lost over R50 million through this vat fraud, while syndicate king pins are making hundreds millions in the process.


UPSOUND LEBELO: The small guys on the bottom that do the zama zama, it’s just moving from hand to mouth kind of a thing. But the main players are the kingpins who are running this thing, at the expense of everybody else.


LINK: It basically boils down to this, every time you buy second hand jewellery chances are you’re contributing to the illegal gold trade.


VO: The HAWKS arrested two suspects, a former police officer Gerrit Bezuidenhout and Susanne Eksteen who were charged with money laundering, forgery and racketeering.
They’re alleged to be part of an illicit gold industry sydindicate that has fabricated over 16 000 fraudulent invoices worth over R437 million, to reflect purchases of second hand gold jewellery.
Hawks spokesperson, Brig Hangwani Mulaudzi says that they’ve been investing this illegal gold mining syndicate for three years.


UPSOUND: Brig Hangwani: 02:56:49 - We have got lots and lots of syndicates that are operating in the country. ...we are just taking it bit by bit ...we are working very hard with SARS and they are also part and parcel of this operation. ... in March we had a similar operation at the time, we did not have any arrests we only had no documents, no computers and all those kind of things.



LINK 18:22:31:00 - It’s estimated that illegal mining costs our economy millions every year but the zama zamas, but the bulk of the money....


UPSOUND LEBELO:
The poor guy on the ground, work day and night under risky conditions...

[11:20] It’s quite big. You cant even compare the two, the kingpins are milking it all.

[12:33] They are living in very luxurious properties, they’re driving very expensive cars, they even own jets some of them, some of them they even own boats, very very expensive boats.


[11:20]


VO:

The Hawks believe that they will be making even more arrests in the coming months.

Meanwhile life at Durban Deep Informal Settlement continues, as hundreds of zama zamas continue to head underground, in search of gold.
